findings.evidence: Step 6: 'The body says why, and `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer marks only a real compatibility break.' This is Conventional Commits basics the model already knows. It is activation content inside an otherwise expert step.

Leave the why-body and breaking-change basics to references/commit-message-template.md § Message template, where they already appear, and add a record row for the trimmed sentence.

findings.evidence: Step 3 ('Stage. Scratch files ... go in a run directory of their own ...') and its four sub-bullets make up about a third of the body. Run-directory lifecycle, index choice, overlap check, temporary-index setup and three staging methods are mixed together, which weakens the Process pattern's checkpoint structure.
findings.fix: Split step 3 into labelled sub-steps without removing any content: 3a run directory (create, list leftovers, cleanup), 3b choose the index (including the overlap check), 3c stage (whole file / part of a tracked file / untracked file). Keep every command and rule as written.

findings.evidence: Eval 'split-one-file-two-commits' lists "references/split-one-file.md" under "files". findings.evidence: Route 'draft a message': 'with none, read-only inspection only (`git status`, `git diff --cached`, `git log`); reply with the message text only'. findings.fix: Add to the draft-a-message row: 'when nothing is staged, say so and draft from `git diff` only if the user confirms that is the change to commit; otherwise ask which changes the message is for.'

findings.evidence: Message template restates the Conventional Commits skeleton `<type>(<scope>): <summary>` plus a what/why body that step 6 already requires.
findings.fix: Keep the skeleton in references/commit-message-template.md (users ask for the template by name); do not delete it. Trim only the duplicate prose if a later edit touches that section, and record any removed sentence in docs/audit/recovery/commit-work/record.md.

findings.evidence: Step 6 gates references/commit-message-template.md on repository rules, extra footers, or wanting worked messages, but also says to read it for the step 8 report block, which step 8 then requires for every commit.
findings.fix: Move the report-block format inline at step 8 (it is six lines) and keep the reference gated on repository message rules, footers beyond BREAKING CHANGE, and worked messages.

findings.evidence: Step 6 says write Conventional Commits 1.0.0 when the repository uses it or has no vocabulary of its own, but does not say how to tell that it uses it, while the reference says to copy `git log --format=%s -30` only when none of the rule files exist.
findings.fix: In step 6, name the default: the repository uses Conventional Commits when a commitlint config, a commit.template, or recent `git log --format=%s -30` subjects already use type(scope); otherwise copy that log's vocabulary. findings.evidence: The should-trigger query "can you check in the tests for the parser separately from the parser change itself?" asks for the split the skill's opening rule forbids (implementation and its tests in one commit).

findings.evidence: Eighteen evals assert command sequences, but none checks the step 4 overlap case: an approved path that already holds a staged diff the user did not approve, where the skill must stop and never run the step 8 git reset.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose fixture shows an approved path with an unapproved staged hunk plus other approved files, asserting a stop, no git apply or git add over that path, and no git reset on it.

findings.evidence: Step 6's "or has no vocabulary of its own" contradicts references/commit-message-template.md, which says that with no rule files you copy `git log --format=%s -30` rather than default to Conventional Commits.
findings.fix: Make step 6 defer to the reference whenever commitlint, commit.template, CONTRIBUTING, a PR template, or recent subjects exist, and default to Conventional Commits only when those sources are absent; the reference's collect step already says to ask when two sources conflict.

findings.evidence: After the first commit, step 6 says `git add -- src/components/Header.js` stages the rest of the file, but a temporary index was built from the old HEAD and still lacks the bugfix commit, so that add would stage the refactor against a stale tree.
findings.fix: State the order as a requirement: in temporary-index mode, rebuild with `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<run>/index git read-tree HEAD` (and re-copy any approved staged patches) before `git add -- src/components/Header.js`; only the real-index route may add the rest immediately.

findings.evidence: Description lists sx, Grid size, slots, createTheme, CSS variables, colorSchemes, Dialog onClose, Skeleton and IconButton, but not the styled and styleOverrides state-class work in resources/styling-guide.md.
findings.fix: Use when writing, fixing or migrating React code on Material UI v7 (@mui/material, @mui/icons-material, @mui/material/styles): sx styling and its spacing and borderRadius multipliers, Grid size layouts, slots/slotProps, createTheme palettes and color augmentation, CSS variables, colorSchemes dark mode, CSS layers, Dialog onClose, Skeleton loading, IconButton names, and styled or styleOverrides that must beat a MUI state class. Trigger when upgrading v5 or v6 code (onBackdropClick, Grid item/xs/md, components/componentsProps, deep imports) or editing an existing MUI screen, even when the user does not say v7. Not for Joy UI, MUI X data grids or pickers, Base UI, Chakra UI, Vuetify, Radix, a native <dialog>, Tailwind-only or plain CSS styling, or general React setup.
